  FROM fct_order_lines ol
  JOIN dim_country dc ON ol.country_key = dc.country_key
  WHERE dc.country_name = 'United Kingdom'
    AND ol.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
    AND ol.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
total_2011_revenue AS (
  SELECT SUM(ol.line_revenue) AS total_net_revenue
  FROM fct_order_lines ol
  WHERE ol.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'

)
SELECT

  total_2011_revenue.total_net_revenue,

FROM uk_revenue, total_2011_revenue

sql.sql:
SELECT 
    d.date_key,
    d.date_day,
    d.calendar_year,
    d.month_name,
    SUM(f.line_revenue) AS daily_net_revenue
FROM fct_order_lines f
JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN dim_date d ON d.date_key = f.date_key
WHERE p.is_merchandise 
  AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
  AND d.calendar_year = 2011
  AND d.month_name = 'November'
GROUP BY d.date_key, d.date_day, d.calendar_year, d.month_name
ORDER BY d.date_key

SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS n_trading_days,
    SUM(daily_net_revenue) AS total_net_revenue
FROM (
    SELECT 
        d.date_key,
        d.date_day,
        d.calendar_year,
        d.month_name,
        SUM(f.line_revenue) AS daily_net_revenue
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.date_key = f.date_key
    WHERE p.is_merchandise 
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND d.calendar_year = 2011
      AND d.month_name = 'November'
    GROUP BY d.date_key, d.date_day, d.calendar_year, d.month_name
) AS daily_revenue

SELECT 
    ROUND(SUM(daily_net_revenue) / COUNT(*), 2) AS avg_net_revenue_per_trading_day
FROM (
    SELECT 
        d.date_key,
        d.date_day,
        d.calendar_year,
        d.month_name,
        SUM(f.line_revenue) AS daily_net_revenue
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_date d ON d.date_key = f.date_key
    WHERE p.is_merchandise 
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND d.calendar_year = 2011
      AND d.month_name = 'November'
    GROUP BY d.date_key, d.date_day, d.calendar_year, d.month_name
) AS daily_revenue

WITH nov2010 AS (
  SELECT

  FROM fct_order_lines
  JOIN dim_product ON fct_order_lines.product_key = dim_product.product_key
  JOIN dim_customer ON fct_order_lines.customer_sk = dim_customer.customer_sk
  JOIN dim_country ON fct_order_lines.country_key = dim_country.country_key

  GROUP BY dim_country.country_name, dim_customer.loyalty_tier
),
nov2011 AS (
  SELECT 
    dim_country.country_name,
    dim_customer.loyalty_tier,
    SUM(fct_order_lines.line_revenue) AS tier_revenue
  FROM fct_order_lines
  JOIN dim_product ON fct_order_lines.product_key = dim_product.product_key
  JOIN dim_customer ON fct_order_lines.customer_sk = dim_customer.customer_sk
  JOIN dim_country ON fct_order_lines.country_key = dim_country.country_key
  WHERE dim_country.country_name = 'United Kingdom'
    AND dim_product.is_merchandise = true

  GROUP BY dim_country.country_name, dim_customer.loyalty_tier
),
combined AS (
  SELECT 
    nov2010.country_name,
    nov2010.loyalty_tier,
    nov2010.tier_revenue AS nov2010_revenue,
    nov2011.tier_revenue AS nov2011_revenue,
    nov2011.tier_revenue - nov2010.tier_revenue AS tier_change
  FROM nov2010
  JOIN nov2011 ON nov2010.country_name = nov2011.country_name AND nov2010.loyalty_tier = nov2011.loyalty_tier
),
totals AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(nov2010_revenue) AS nov2010_total,
    SUM(nov2011_revenue) AS nov2011_total
  FROM combined
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT 
    *,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY tier_change DESC) AS change_rank
  FROM combined
)
SELECT 
  nov2010_total AS nov2010_uk_total,
  nov2011_total AS nov2011_uk_total,
  nov2011_total - nov2010_total AS uk_total_change,
  tier_change,
  loyalty_tier,
  change_rank
FROM ranked
JOIN totals ON 1=1
ORDER BY change_rank

WITH uk_sales AS (
  SELECT 
    f.invoice_ts,
    d.country_name,
    c.loyalty_tier,
    f.line_revenue
  FROM fct_order_lines f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
  JOIN dim_country d ON f.country_key = d.country_key
  WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
    AND d.country_name = 'United Kingdom'
    AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-11-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2011-12-01'
),
monthly_totals AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_ts) AS month,
    SUM(line_revenue) AS monthly_net_revenue
  FROM uk_sales
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_ts)
),
tier_monthly AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_ts) AS month,
    loyalty_tier,
    SUM(line_revenue) AS tier_revenue
  FROM uk_sales
  GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', invoice_ts), loyalty_tier
),
tier_monthly_change AS (
  SELECT 
    t1.month,
    t1.loyalty_tier,
    t1.tier_revenue,
    t2.tier_revenue AS prev_tier_revenue,
    t1.tier_revenue - t2.tier_revenue AS tier_change
  FROM tier_monthly t1
  LEFT JOIN tier_monthly t2 ON t1.month = DATE_ADD(month, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AND t1.loyalty_tier = t2.loyalty_tier
)
SELECT

  mt.monthly_net_revenue,
  tmc.tier_change,

answer: The sales region that grew its net merchandise revenue the most in absolute terms from 2010 to 2011 is **Asia Pacific**, with an absolute growth of **£128,085.06**. Its two annual totals were **£54,468.19** in 2010 and **£182,553.25** in 2011 (partial year ending 9 December). [q1]

sql.sql:
WITH region_2010 AS (
  SELECT 
    d.region,
    SUM(f.merchandise_revenue) AS net_revenue_2010
  FROM fct_orders f
  JOIN dim_country d ON f.country_key = d.country_key
  WHERE f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
    AND d.region IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY d.region
),
region_2011 AS (
  SELECT 
    d.region,
    SUM(f.merchandise_revenue) AS net_revenue_2011
  FROM fct_orders f
  JOIN dim_country d ON f.country_key = d.country_key
  WHERE f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2011-12-09'
    AND d.region IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY d.region
)
SELECT 
  r2010.region,
  r2010.net_revenue_2010,
  r2011.net_revenue_2011,
  (r2011.net_revenue_2011 - r2010.net_revenue_2010) AS absolute_growth
FROM region_2010 r2010
JOIN region_2011 r2011 ON r2010.region = r2011.region
ORDER BY absolute_growth DESC
LIMIT 10

sql.sql:
SELECT 
    c.country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2010,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2011,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) - 
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_change
FROM fct_order_lines f
JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
    AND c.country_name != 'United Kingdom'
GROUP BY c.country_name
ORDER BY revenue_change DESC

SELECT 
    dc.country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fct_orders.date_key >= 20100101 AND fct_orders.date_key < 20110101 THEN fct_orders.invoice_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2010,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fct_orders.date_key >= 20110101 AND fct_orders.date_key <= 20111209 THEN fct_orders.invoice_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_2011,
    (SUM(CASE WHEN fct_orders.date_key >= 20110101 AND fct_orders.date_key <= 20111209 THEN fct_orders.invoice_revenue ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN fct_orders.date_key >= 20100101 AND fct_orders.date_key < 20110101 THEN fct_orders.invoice_revenue ELSE 0 END)) AS growth

answer: In 2011, the average order value (AOV) for customers in the platinum tier was **£898.23**, while for customers in the bronze tier it was **£197.28**. The platinum tier AOV was **4.55 times** higher than the bronze tier AOV.

sql.sql:
WITH platinum_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        f.invoice_id,
        f.invoice_revenue,
        f.total_units,
        f.customer_sk,
        f.invoice_ts
    FROM fct_orders f
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE c.loyalty_tier = 'platinum'
        AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
        AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
bronze_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        f.invoice_id,
        f.invoice_revenue,
        f.total_units,
        f.customer_sk,
        f.invoice_ts
    FROM fct_orders f
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE c.loyalty_tier = 'bronze'
        AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
        AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
platinum_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(invoice_revenue) AS total_revenue,
        SUM(total_units) AS total_units,
        COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_id) AS n_orders
    FROM platinum_orders
),
bronze_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(invoice_revenue) AS total_revenue,
        SUM(total_units) AS total_units,
        COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_id) AS n_orders
    FROM bronze_orders
)
SELECT 
    p.total_revenue / p.n_orders AS platinum_aov,
    b.total_revenue / b.n_orders AS bronze_aov,
    (p.total_revenue / p.n_orders) / (b.total_revenue / b.n_orders) AS ratio
FROM platinum_stats p, bronze_stats b;

answer: In 2011, the average order value for customers in the platinum tier was **£35.31 [q1]**, while for customers in the bronze tier it was **£7.27 [q1]**. The platinum tier AOV was **4.86 times higher** than the bronze tier AOV [q2].

sql.sql:
WITH 
  -- Get all invoices in 2011 with their customer tier at the time of sale
  invoices_with_tier AS (
    SELECT 
      o.invoice_id,
      o.customer_sk,
      o.invoice_ts,
      o.invoice_revenue,
      o.total_units,
      c.loyalty_tier
    FROM fct_orders o
    JOIN dim_customer c ON o.customer_sk = c.customer_sk 
      AND c.valid_from <= o.invoice_ts 
      AND c.valid_to > o.invoice_ts
    WHERE o.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND o.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
  ),
  -- Calculate AOV by tier
  tier_aov AS (
    SELECT 
      loyalty_tier,
      SUM(invoice_revenue) AS total_revenue,
      COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_id) AS n_orders,
      AVG(invoice_revenue * 1.0 / NULLIF(total_units, 0)) AS aov
    FROM invoices_with_tier
    WHERE loyalty_tier IN ('platinum', 'bronze')
    GROUP BY loyalty_tier
  )
  SELECT 
    loyalty_tier,
    ROUND(aov, 2) AS aov_gbp,
    n_orders,
    total_revenue
  FROM tier_aov
  ORDER BY aov_gbp DESC;

answer: In 2011, the average order value (AOV) for customers in the platinum tier was **£1,170.62 [q1]**, while for customers in the bronze tier it was **£289.35 [q1]**. The ratio of the platinum AOV to the bronze AOV was approximately **4.05 [q1]**, meaning platinum customers spent about four times more per order than bronze customers.

sql.sql:
WITH platinum_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        f.invoice_id,
        f.customer_sk,
        f.invoice_ts,
        f.merchandise_revenue,
        f.total_units,
        f.line_type
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE p.is_merchandise = true
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND c.loyalty_tier = 'platinum'
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
platinum_invoices AS (
    SELECT 
        invoice_id,
        SUM(merchandise_revenue) AS total_merchandise_revenue,
        SUM(total_units) AS total_units,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN line_type = 'sale' THEN invoice_id END) AS n_sales
    FROM platinum_orders
    GROUP BY invoice_id
),
platinum_aov AS (
    SELECT 
        total_merchandise_revenue / n_sales AS aov_platinum
    FROM platinum_invoices
    WHERE n_sales > 0
),
bronze_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        f.invoice_id,
        f.customer_sk,
        f.invoice_ts,
        f.merchandise_revenue,
        f.total_units,
        f.line_type
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE p.is_merchandise = true
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND c.loyalty_tier = 'bronze'
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
bronze_invoices AS (
    SELECT 
        invoice_id,
        SUM(merchandise_revenue) AS total_merchandise_revenue,
        SUM(total_units) AS total_units,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN line_type = 'sale' THEN invoice_id END) AS n_sales
    FROM bronze_orders
    GROUP BY invoice_id
),
bronze_aov AS (
    SELECT 
        total_merchandise_revenue / n_sales AS aov_bronze
    FROM bronze_invoices
    WHERE n_sales > 0
)
SELECT 
    aov_platinum,
    aov_bronze,
    aov_platinum / aov_bronze AS ratio
FROM platinum_aov
CROSS JOIN bronze_aov;

WITH platinum_invoices AS (
    SELECT 
        f.invoice_id,
        f.merchandise_revenue,
        f.total_units,
        f.invoice_ts,
        f.customer_sk
    FROM fct_orders f
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE c.loyalty_tier = 'platinum'
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
      AND f.invoice_type = 'sale'
),
platinum_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        SUM(merchandise_revenue) AS total_revenue,

        COUNT(*) AS n_orders
    FROM platinum_invoices
),
bronze_invoices AS (

    WHERE c.loyalty_tier = 'bronze'
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
      AND f.invoice_type = 'sale'
),
bronze_agg AS (

SELECT

    (p.total_revenue / p.n_orders) / (b.total_revenue / b.n_orders) AS ratio
FROM platinum_agg p

answer: September 2011 net merchandise revenue grew by 20.17% year over year [q2]. This growth was primarily driven by a higher average order value (AOV), not by more orders. In September 2010, there were 1,911 orders with an AOV of £440.38 [q2]. In September 2011, there were 1,896 orders with an AOV of £533.41 [q2]. The order count decreased by 0.78% [q2], while the AOV increased by 21.12% [q2]. The revenue growth was driven by customers spending more per order rather than ordering more frequently.

answer:
Based on the query results:

- **September 2010**: 1,911 orders, AOV £440.38 [q2]
- **September 2011**: 1,896 orders, AOV £533.41 [q2]
- **Order growth rate**: -0.78% (orders decreased from 1,911 to 1,896) [q2]
- **AOV difference**: £93.03 (AOV increased from £440.38 to £533.41) [q2]
- **AOV growth rate**: +21.12% [q2]
- **YoY net merchandise revenue growth**: +20.17% [q2]

The year-over-year revenue growth was driven primarily by a **higher average order value**, not more orders. Orders slightly decreased by 0.78%, while AOV increased by £93.03 (21.12%). The 20.17% revenue growth was achieved despite fewer orders, entirely due to the substantial increase in average order value.

sql.sql:
SELECT 
    revenue_month,
    n_orders,
    avg_order_value,
    yoy_growth
FROM mart_revenue_monthly
WHERE revenue_month IN ('2010-09', '2011-09')
ORDER BY revenue_month

SELECT 
    revenue_month,
    n_orders,
    avg_order_value,
    yoy_growth
FROM mart_revenue_monthly
WHERE revenue_month >= '2010-09-01' AND revenue_month < '2010-10-01'
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    revenue_month,
    n_orders,
    avg_order_value,
    yoy_growth
FROM mart_revenue_monthly
WHERE revenue_month >= '2011-09-01' AND revenue_month < '2011-10-01'
ORDER BY revenue_month

WITH sep_2010 AS (
    SELECT 
        revenue_month,
        n_orders,
        avg_order_value,
        yoy_growth
    FROM mart_revenue_monthly
    WHERE revenue_month >= '2010-09-01' AND revenue_month < '2010-10-01'
),
sep_2011 AS (
    SELECT 
        revenue_month,
        n_orders,
        avg_order_value,
        yoy_growth
    FROM mart_revenue_monthly
    WHERE revenue_month >= '2011-09-01' AND revenue_month < '2011-10-01'
)
SELECT 
    s2010.n_orders AS orders_2010,
    s2010.avg_order_value AS aov_2010,
    s2011.n_orders AS orders_2011,
    s2011.avg_order_value AS aov_2011,
    s2011.yoy_growth AS yoy_growth,
    (s2011.n_orders * 1.0 / s2010.n_orders - 1) AS order_growth_rate,
    (s2011.avg_order_value - s2010.avg_order_value) AS aov_difference,
    (s2011.avg_order_value * 1.0 / s2010.avg_order_value - 1) AS aov_growth_rate
FROM sep_2010 s2010, sep_2011 s2011

sql.sql:
WITH daily_orders AS (
  SELECT 
    d.date_key,
    d.day_of_week_iso,
    d.day_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN p.is_merchandise AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation') THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS net_revenue,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.invoice_id END) AS n_orders
  FROM fct_order_lines f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_date d ON f.date_key = d.date_key
  WHERE f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
  GROUP BY d.date_key, d.day_of_week_iso, d.day_name
),
daily_aov AS (
  SELECT 
    day_of_week_iso,
    day_name,
    SUM(net_revenue) / SUM(n_orders) AS aov
  FROM daily_orders
  WHERE n_orders > 0
  GROUP BY day_of_week_iso, day_name
)
SELECT * FROM daily_aov ORDER BY day_of_week_iso

In 2011, the cancellation rate by value for UK customers was **5.35%** (428,750.21 GBP in cancelled merchandise divided by 8,019,210.82 GBP in gross merchandise sales) [q1], while the combined cancellation rate by value for all other countries was **2.04%** (29,603.09 GBP in cancelled merchandise divided by 1,452,370.14 GBP in gross merchandise sales) [q3].

sql.sql:
SELECT 
    country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_merchandise,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS gross_merchandise_sales,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancellation_rate_value
FROM fct_order_lines f
JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' 
    AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
    AND c.country_name = 'United Kingdom'
GROUP BY c.country_name

SELECT 
    country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_merchandise,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS gross_merchandise_sales,
    -SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) / SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancellation_rate_value
FROM fct_order_lines f
JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' 
    AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
    AND c.country_name != 'United Kingdom'
GROUP BY c.country_name

SELECT 
    SUM(cancelled_merchandise) AS total_cancelled_merchandise,
    SUM(gross_merchandise_sales) AS total_gross_merchandise_sales,
    -SUM(cancelled_merchandise) / SUM(gross_merchandise_sales) AS total_cancellation_rate_value
FROM (
    SELECT 
        country_name,
        SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_merchandise,
        SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS gross_merchandise_sales
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
    WHERE p.is_merchandise 
        AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' 
        AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
        AND c.country_name != 'United Kingdom'
    GROUP BY c.country_name
) sub

WITH uk_data AS (
  SELECT 
    -SUM(CASE WHEN fct_order_lines.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN fct_order_lines.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS uk_cancelled_merchandise,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fct_order_lines.line_type = 'sale' THEN fct_order_lines.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS uk_gross_merchandise_sales
  FROM fct_order_lines
  JOIN dim_product ON fct_order_lines.product_key = dim_product.product_key
  JOIN dim_country ON fct_order_lines.country_key = dim_country.country_key
  WHERE dim_country.country_name = 'United Kingdom'
    AND dim_product.is_merchandise = TRUE
    AND fct_order_lines.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
    AND fct_order_lines.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
),
other_data AS (
  SELECT 
    -SUM(CASE WHEN fct_order_lines.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN fct_order_lines.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS other_cancelled_merchandise,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fct_order_lines.line_type = 'sale' THEN fct_order_lines.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS other_gross_merchandise_sales
  FROM fct_order_lines
  JOIN dim_product ON fct_order_lines.product_key = dim_product.product_key
  JOIN dim_country ON fct_order_lines.country_key = dim_country.country_key
  WHERE dim_country.country_name != 'United Kingdom'
    AND dim_product.is_merchandise = TRUE
    AND fct_order_lines.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01'
    AND fct_order_lines.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
)
SELECT 
  uk_cancelled_merchandise / uk_gross_merchandise_sales * 100 AS uk_cancellation_rate_pct,
  other_cancelled_merchandise / other_gross_merchandise_sales * 100 AS other_cancellation_rate_pct,
  uk_cancelled_merchandise,
  uk_gross_merchandise_sales,
  other_cancelled_merchandise,
  other_gross_merchandise_sales
FROM uk_data, other_data;

sql.sql:
WITH country_2011 AS (
  SELECT 
    c.country_key,
    c.country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS gross_merchandise_sales,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_merchandise
  FROM fct_order_lines f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
  WHERE f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
    AND p.is_merchandise = true
    AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
  GROUP BY c.country_key, c.country_name
  HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) > 50000
),
cancellation_rates AS (
  SELECT

WITH country_gross AS (
  SELECT 
    c.country_key,
    c.country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'sale' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS gross_merchandise_sales
  FROM fct_order_lines f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
  WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.line_type = 'sale'
    AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.country_key, c.country_name
),
country_cancelled AS (
  SELECT 
    c.country_key,
    c.country_name,
    SUM(CASE WHEN f.line_type = 'cancellation' THEN f.line_revenue ELSE 0 END) AS cancelled_merchandise
  FROM fct_order_lines f
  JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
  JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key
  WHERE p.is_merchandise 
    AND f.line_type = 'cancellation'
    AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2011-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2012-01-01'
  GROUP BY c.country_key, c.country_name
),
country_metrics AS (
  SELECT 
    c.country_key,
    c.country_name,
    COALESCE(g.gross_merchandise_sales, 0) AS gross_merchandise_sales,
    COALESCE(can.cancelled_merchandise, 0) AS cancelled_merchandise
  FROM dim_country c
  LEFT JOIN country_gross g ON c.country_key = g.country_key
  LEFT JOIN country_cancelled can ON c.country_key = can.country_key
)
SELECT 
  country_name,
  gross_merchandise_sales,
  cancelled_merchandise,
  CASE WHEN gross_merchandise_sales > 0 
    THEN -cancelled_merchandise / gross_merchandise_sales 
    ELSE NULL END AS cancellation_rate_by_value
FROM country_metrics
WHERE gross_merchandise_sales > 50000
ORDER BY cancellation_rate_by_value DESC
LIMIT 10

),

    WHERE p.is_merchandise

    GROUP BY f.customer_id
),

    ROUND(SUM(c.customer_net_revenue) * 100.0 / t.total_net_revenue_2011, 2) AS top_5_share_pct

GROUP BY t.total_net_revenue_2011

For 2010, the net merchandise revenue from customers who were **platinum at the time of sale** was **£1,695,465.67 [q2]**, while the same figure measured by their **current tier** (as of the end of the data window) was **£2,857,092.13 [q2]**.

sql.sql:
WITH 
  -- Net merchandise revenue by historical tier (tier at time of sale) for 2010
  historical_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
      p.loyalty_tier AS tier,
      SUM(f.line_revenue) AS net_revenue
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_sk = c.customer_sk
    WHERE p.is_merchandise 
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2010-12-31 23:59:59'
    GROUP BY p.loyalty_tier
  ),
  
  -- Net merchandise revenue by current tier (tier as of end of 2010) for 2010
  current_revenue AS (
    SELECT 
      c.loyalty_tier AS tier,
      SUM(f.line_revenue) AS net_revenue
    FROM fct_order_lines f
    JOIN dim_product p ON f.product_key = p.product_key
    JOIN dim_customer c ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id AND c.is_current = true
    WHERE p.is_merchandise 
      AND f.line_type IN ('sale', 'cancellation')
      AND f.invoice_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2010-01-01' AND f.invoice_ts < TIMESTAMP '2010-12-31 23:59:59'
    GROUP BY c.loyalty_tier
  ),
  
  -- Total net merchandise revenue for 2010
  total_revenue AS (
    SELECT SUM(net_revenue) AS total
    FROM (
      SELECT SUM(net_revenue) AS net_revenue
      FROM historical_revenue
      UNION ALL
      SELECT SUM(net_revenue) AS net_revenue
      FROM current_revenue
    )
  )
  
  SELECT 
    h.tier AS historical_tier,
    h.net_revenue AS historical_revenue,
    c.net_revenue AS current_revenue,
    h.net_revenue - c.net_revenue AS difference
  FROM historical_revenue h
  FULL OUTER JOIN current_revenue c ON h.tier = c.tier
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    'Total' AS historical_tier,
    (SELECT SUM(net_revenue) FROM historical_revenue) AS historical_revenue,
    (SELECT SUM(net_revenue) FROM current_revenue) AS current_revenue,
    (SELECT SUM(net_revenue) FROM historical_revenue) - (SELECT SUM(net_revenue) FROM current_revenue) AS difference
  ;

The customer tier history changes the picture by **£3,368,826.87**, with the historical tier measurement showing lower revenue than the current tier measurement for 2010.

    JOIN dim_country c ON f.country_key = c.country_key

    GROUP BY f.customer_id

total AS (
    SELECT SUM(customer_revenue) AS total_net_revenue FROM dutch_orders

ranked AS (
